description: The Frame-scale vehicle roster a personnel-scale kid can crew, per design/scale-and-chassis.md. All five are Chassis Level 12, rising automatically with the Frames (12->20). Every stat here is transcribed from that document's §6/§8a, not decided here -- treat design/scale-and-chassis.md as the source of truth for the maths and this file as its data form.

chassis.name: "Kingfisher" Pursuit Coupe
chassis.subtitle: the sports car
chassis.acquisition: Directorate fleet asset -- decided 2026-09-09: shown to players openly, no purchase, freely swappable with the rest of the roster. Not commandeered or negotiated for (that was an open question in §13; this resolves it for now, pending confirmation).
chassis.space: 15 ft long, 8 ft wide, 5 ft high

handlingDC.basis: civilian build; twitchy, never meant for this

vision.description: wide angle, moderate range. Nothing is in the way.

specialAbilities.name: Open-topped
specialAbilities.description: Occupants get lesser cover only (standard cover against attackers at ground level).

specialAbilities.name: Outrun
specialAbilities.description: If the pilot spends their entire turn on Drive actions, the coupe cannot be targeted by reactions triggered by its movement.

chassis.flavorText: Trades durability for reach and sight: it crosses the map in a round, reliably takes zero damage from a near miss, and can actually see what it's driving past.

damageStates.operational: 100-67% HP -- no penalty, Resonance/Handling governs as normal.
damageStates.degraded: 66-34% HP -- -2 AC/saves, x3/4 Speed, capped at 2 actions regardless of Resonance band.
damageStates.critical: 33-1% HP -- -4 AC/saves (matches RAW Broken), x1/2 Speed, x1/2 Hardness, capped at 1 action.

chassis.name: "Hod" Armoured Carrier
chassis.subtitle: the APC
chassis.acquisition: Directorate fleet asset -- decided 2026-09-09: shown to players openly, no purchase, freely swappable with the rest of the roster.
chassis.space: 25 ft long, 10 ft wide, 10 ft high

handlingDC.basis: built to be driven by anyone who's had one lesson

vision.description: narrow angle, short range. Buttoned up; you are looking through a slit.

specialAbilities.name: Enclosed
specialAbilities.description: Occupants have greater cover, and cannot be targeted by Frame-scale area effects at all while the carrier is above its Broken Threshold.

specialAbilities.name: Firing Ports
specialAbilities.description: Up to two passengers may make personnel-scale attacks without losing greater cover.

chassis.flavorText: The mobile safe square. Slow enough that where you park it is a real commitment -- and blind enough that parking it well requires somebody else's eyes.

damageStates.operational: 100-67% HP -- no penalty, Resonance/Handling governs as normal.
damageStates.degraded: 66-34% HP -- -2 AC/saves, x3/4 Speed, capped at 2 actions regardless of Resonance band.
damageStates.critical: 33-1% HP -- -4 AC/saves (matches RAW Broken), x1/2 Speed, x1/2 Hardness, capped at 1 action.

chassis.name: "Ladle" Recovery Rig
chassis.subtitle: field repair
chassis.acquisition: Directorate fleet asset -- decided 2026-09-09: shown to players openly, no purchase, freely swappable with the rest of the roster.
chassis.space: 25 ft long, 12 ft wide, 11 ft high

specialAbilities.name: Field Repair
specialAbilities.description: Two actions, a crew member, requires the rig adjacent to a Frame: Crafting check against the rig's own Handling DC (16) -- a personnel-scale DC, per the scale interface's second legal conversion. Critical success restores 40 HP to the Frame; success restores 25; failure restores 10; critical failure restores nothing and Marks the rig. The cost, and the point: every point restored this way is borrowed against the shared technician-day pool in config.json's Frame economy -- it doesn't create capability, it moves it forward in time. Spending next week's repair budget to survive tonight.

damageStates.operational: 100-67% HP -- no penalty, Resonance/Handling governs as normal.
damageStates.degraded: 66-34% HP -- -2 AC/saves, x3/4 Speed, capped at 2 actions regardless of Resonance band.
damageStates.critical: 33-1% HP -- -4 AC/saves (matches RAW Broken), x1/2 Speed, x1/2 Hardness, capped at 1 action.

chassis.notes: How much technician-day debt one Field Repair actually costs is design/scale-and-chassis.md §13's still-open question 2 -- a dial to be set alongside config.json's Frame economy numbers, not decided here.

chassis.name: "Vesper" Observation Helicopter
chassis.subtitle: the glass cockpit
chassis.acquisition: Directorate fleet asset -- decided 2026-09-09: shown to players openly, no purchase, freely swappable with the rest of the roster.
chassis.space: 30 ft long, 10 ft wide, 12 ft high

handlingDC.basis: the hardest thing on the roster to fly

vision.description: long range, wide angle, unobstructed. Altitude and glass.

specialAbilities.name: Falls
specialAbilities.description: Per RAW, a destroyed flying vehicle falls and everyone aboard takes falling damage. This is the real price of the helicopter and should never be softened.

chassis.flavorText: By far the greatest speed, the lowest Hardness, high Reflex, critically low Fortitude. That last one has teeth, because Fortitude is a vehicle's default save under RAW -- anything that doesn't target Reflex targets the helicopter's worst number. It survives roughly as many area attacks as the others (~4.8), but it is the only chassis where losing that gamble also drops the crew out of the sky.

chassis.name: "Runabout" Utility Chassis
chassis.subtitle: always available, no stakes
chassis.acquisition: Directorate-issued, replaced on request -- not meaningfully purchased or lost from a player's economy at all. Exists specifically so a player is never mechanically locked out of the vehicle layer, and so throwing one away tactically is always an option with a floor under it.
chassis.space: 14 ft long, 7 ft wide, 6 ft high

handlingDC.basis: reliable, unglamorous, exactly as easy to fly as it needs to be and no easier

chassis.flavorText: Deliberately mediocre on every axis rather than specialized on any -- the point is not that it's a good option, the point is that it is always an option. A Runabout survives roughly 2 area attacks (vs. the named chassis' ~5), which is correct: losing one should sting less than being caught without a vehicle at all, and should sting less than losing a Kingfisher.
